1: # AGENTS.md — 01_Ideas

3: Raw, unstructured concept capture. Low friction — just enough context to remember.

5: ## Why have ideas?
6: 
7: To capture every thought about the homelab before it's lost. Ideas are the seed of the pipeline — no idea is too small or too vague.
8: 
9: ## When to create
10: 
11: Any thought about new tech, homelab changes, or wishlist items.
12: 
13: ## Status Lifecycle
14: 
15: ```
16: draft → accepted
17:   L__> archived → (move to 06_Archive/ideas/)
18: ```
19: 
20: - **draft**: Just captured
21: - **accepted**: Worth pursuing
22: - **archived**: Discarded or superseded
23: 
24: ## File system layout
25: 
26: ```
27: 01_Ideas/{topic}/
28: ├── idea-{name}.md     # one per specific idea
29: ├── idea-notes.md      # scratchpad, raw thoughts, links
30: └── overview.md        # high-level summary of the topic area
31: ```
32: 
33: All names in kebab-case. Multiple files per topic allowed. Use the atomic rule (150 lines) to decide when to split.
34: 
35: ## Frontmatter (required)
36: 
37: ```yaml
38: ---
39: title: ""
40: status: draft        # draft | accepted | archived
41: author: ""
42: date: YYYY-MM-DD
43: tags: []
44: technologies: []
45: related_ideas: []
46: ---
47: ```
48:

50: 
51: ```yaml
52: ---
53: title: "Move databases to separate node"
54: status: draft
55: author: "padawont"
56: date: 2026-08-13
57: tags: [databases, performance, architecture]
58: technologies: [postgresql, mysql, mariadb]
59: related_ideas: []
60: ---
61: ```
62: 
63: See `./Templates/ideas/idea.md` for a copyable template.
64: 
65: ## Structure
66: 
67: No strict structure — freeform markdown. The template provides a starting point.
68: 
69: ## Conventions
70: 
71: - No formal review needed for `draft → accepted`
72: - No stale timeout — ideas live indefinitely
73: - When `accepted`, the idea is ready — optionally create a Knowledge note
74: - Use `idea-notes.md` for loose thoughts that don't warrant their own file

---
title: "Expose NAS only through a zero-trust proxy"
status: draft
author: "padawont"
date: 2026-10-21
tags: [zero-trust, remote-access, security]
technologies: [cloudflare-access, tailscale, authentik, nginx]
related_ideas: []
---

# Expose NAS only through a zero-trust proxy

## Objective

Reach the NAS from outside the LAN without opening any inbound ports. All access
goes through an identity-aware proxy that authenticates the user before any
request reaches the NAS, and applies policy per app rather than to the whole box.

## Access model

- **Identity-aware proxy**: every request is authenticated (SSO/MFA) at the
  proxy; unauthenticated traffic never reaches the NAS.
- **No port forwards**: nothing published on the router; the proxy reaches the
  NAS over an outbound tunnel from inside the LAN.
- **Per-app policy**: each NAS service (file share, admin UI, media) gets its
  own access rule and allowed identity group instead of one shared door.

## Open Questions

- Which proxy fits best — self-hosted (Authentik + Nginx) or managed (Cloudflare Access)?
- Can per-app policy be expressed cleanly for the admin UI versus read-only shares?
- How does the tunnel terminate on the NAS versus on a small in-LAN relay?
